factors.name: Size
factors.summary: Number of duplicate tasks, Size and Token split load very highly (0.95–0.97), so the factor captures how large the net is, including repeated or silent transitions and outgoing arcs. Density (-0.58) and Average connector degree (-0.48) load negatively, consistent with larger nets being sparser; both cross-load on Factor 3.

factors.name: Connector degree / connectivity
factors.summary: Maximum connector degree dominates (0.95), with Coefficient of network connectivity (0.66) and Average connector degree (0.46, cross-loading) adding to it. The factor reflects how many arcs meet at connectors and arcs per node. The loading of Maximum connector degree sits at a possible Heywood case, so the factor may be partly driven by a single measure.

factors.name: Connector homogeneity and density
factors.summary: Connector Heterogeneity loads strongly negatively (-0.93), together with positive loadings of Density (0.61) and Average connector degree (0.58), both of which cross-load on Factor 1. Nets that score high use mostly one connector type and are relatively dense; the combination has no single established name, so the interpretation is tentative.

factors.name: Separability
factors.summary: Only Separability is assigned (0.63), with moderate secondary loadings of Coefficient of network connectivity (0.48), Average connector degree (0.41) and Density (0.40) below the assignment rule. Its eigenvalue (0.71) is below 1 and it explains about 11% of the variance, so it is a weak factor carried by one measure.

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO (0.75) exceeds 0.6, so the data are suitable for factor analysis. The four varimax factors explain 85% of the variance. However, only two eigenvalues exceed 1 and two factors were suggested. The clearest dimension is size (Factor 1), followed by connector degree/connectivity (Factor 2). Factors 3 and 4 are weaker and partly built on cross-loading measures. Density and Average connector degree spread over several factors, and Connector Mismatch remains unassigned due to low communality (0.21).
caveats: Four factors were extracted although only two eigenvalues exceed 1 and two were suggested, so Factors 3 and 4 may be over-extraction.
Maximum connector degree has a communality at the bound of the fit (possible Heywood case), which makes Factor 2 less reliable.
Average connector degree and Density cross-load on several factors, blurring the separation between size, connectivity and density.
Connector Mismatch is unassigned because of low communality.
Sequentiality and Control flow complexity were removed by the MSA filter and Number of empty sequence flows was constant, so these aspects are not represented.
The results reflect shared variance in these 288 nets under varimax rotation and do not imply causal relations.
